title: Structured entry fee + elastic support pilot for private/VPC and on‑prem
creator: Marcus Rivera
description: Problem: Enterprise prospects repeatedly ask for a predictable entry fee for Private/VPC installs but want flexibility on support level and upgrade timing. Current approaches (flat annual license or purely seat-based contracts) either block smaller deals or force deep discounting. Goal: Validate a two-part packaging construct — (1) a modest non-recurring structured entry fee that covers onboarding, baseline compat, and a 12-month upgrade cadence guarantee; and (2) an 'elastic support' add-on where customers choose a support band (Bronze/Silver/Gold) and may temporarily scale up support credits at time of incidents or major upgrades. We will run a pricing experiment with 8 pilot customers across SMB and mid-market segments to measure conversion velocity, average contract value (ACV), time-to-first-deploy, and legal/security questionnaire friction. Hypothesis: A lower upfront license fee + optional elastic support will increase win-rate for customers who are price-sensitive at purchase but willing to pay for predictable operations later. Success metrics: +20% win-rate in pilot cohort, +15% ACV (with support add-ons), and no more than 1 extra week added to procurement due to SQA (security questionnaire) items. This ticket defines the pricing bands, support tiers, upgrade cadence guarantees, SQA answers mapping, sales playbook, and rollout plan for the pilot.

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Sales pushback on any upfront fee for strategic logos — Mitigation: allow a waiver path for strategic accounts with offsetting term length or additional professional services
Risk: SQA items delay procurement — Mitigation: pre-populate SQA answers and provide a standard evidence package for pilot customers
Risk: Engineering bandwidth for expedited upgrades — Mitigation: quota limit for expedited requests and clear paid add-on pricing to fund support work
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Nov): Design pricing bands, legal template, and SQA stub answers
Phase 1 (Dec): Recruit 8 pilot customers, run onboarding, instrument metrics dashboard
Phase 2 (Jan-Feb): Collect conversion, ACV, time-to-deploy, and SQA friction metrics; adjust pricing bands if conversion < baseline
Phase 3 (Mar): Decide on permanent packaging changes and prepare launch playbook for wider GTM
metrics: Pilot win-rate vs historic comparable deals (target +20%)
Mean procurement time from quote to signed SOW (target <= baseline + 7 days)
Number of SQA items escalated to Security/Legal per pilot (target <= 3 per customer)
Number of expedited upgrade requests and associated revenue
